author: product-requirements-expert
title: Clamp owners page parameter below 1 to first page
summary: GET /owners?page=0 (or any value below 1) currently renders the error page instead of the owner listing. The fix must clamp any page value less than 1 to 1 and return HTTP 200 with the normal owner list.
acceptance_criteria: GET /owners?page=0 returns HTTP 200 and renders the owner listing (first page)
GET /owners?page=-5 returns HTTP 200 and renders the owner listing (first page)
GET /owners?page=1 continues to work as before
GET /owners?page=2 (valid second page) continues to work as before

author: feature-implementer
summary: Clamp page<1 to 1 in OwnerController.processFindForm; GET /owners?page=0 and ?page=-5 now return HTTP 200 with the owner list. Two new tests added; full gradle build (check: tests + checkFormat + checkstyle) green.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Test name givenPageZero_whenGetOwners_thenReturnsOwnerList uses a given/when/then format that matches neither the existing class convention (processFindFormSuccess, processFindFormNoOwnersFound, etc.) nor the project BDD school defined in docs/testing-principles.md § Test Naming (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}). The companion test givenPageBelowOne_whenGetOwners_thenReturnsFirstPageWithOkStatus has the same mismatch. Rename to match the BDD convention the testing principles prescribe.

givenPageZero_whenGetOwners_thenReturnsOwnerList does not assert model().attribute("currentPage", 1), so it does not verify that the page=0 input was actually clamped. The test passes as long as any owner list is returned, which was already true for valid pages. The companion test at line 267 correctly asserts currentPage==1 for page=-5; this test should do the same.
findings.fix: Add .andExpect(model().attribute("currentPage", 1)) to the mockMvc.perform(...) chain in givenPageZero_whenGetOwners_thenReturnsOwnerList (theOwnerListShouldClampPageZeroToFirstPage after rename).

approved_aspects: Clamp logic in processFindForm is correct and minimal — one guard at the top of the method, no structural changes elsewhere
Comment at lines 97-98 explains the why (out-of-range requests rendering the error page) rather than restating the code
givenPageBelowOne test correctly verifies both HTTP 200 status and currentPage==1
No new prohibited suffixes, no naming regressions in production code
Constructor injection retained, no @Autowired annotations introduced

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Both new tests use a given/when/then naming school (`givenPageZero_whenGetOwners_thenReturnsOwnerList`, `givenPageBelowOne_whenGetOwners_thenReturnsFirstPageWithOkStatus`). testing-principles.md § Test Naming mandates `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward. Correct names: `theOwnerListShouldShowFirstPageWhenPageIsZero` and `theOwnerListShouldClampPageBelowOneToFirstPage`.

`givenPageZero_whenGetOwners_thenReturnsOwnerList` asserts HTTP 200 and view name but omits the `currentPage == 1` model attribute assertion that the page=-5 test includes. Page 0 is identically a clamping case; the absence of the assertion means this test does not verify the clamped page value is propagated to the model, leaving one half of the boundary unchecked.
findings.fix: Add `.andExpect(model().attribute("currentPage", 1))` to the perform chain in `givenPageZero_whenGetOwners_thenReturnsOwnerList`, mirroring the page=-5 test.

findings.description: The two new tests cover the same behavior (page parameter below 1 clamped to first page) with two input values (0 and -5). Per the test-review checklist, repetitive cases should use `@ParameterizedTest` with `@CsvSource` instead of copy-paste tests. Collapsing them into one parameterized test removes duplication and makes it easier to add further boundary values (e.g., Integer.MIN_VALUE) without a new test method.
findings.fix: Merge the two tests into a single `@ParameterizedTest @CsvSource({"0", "-5"})` method named `theOwnerListShouldClampPageBelowOneToFirstPage(int page)` that asserts status 200, currentPage==1, and the ownersList view for each value.

author: doc-reviewer

REQ-OWN-002 covers owner search and paged listing but none of its Done-when bullets or edge cases address what happens when the page parameter is out of range. The prd-entry record in the handoff log uses req_id REQ-OWNERS-001, a requirement that does not exist in docs/prd.md.
